'''George Grüner''' is a [[Hungarian people|Hungarian]]-[[Americans|American]] [[physicist]] and Distinguished Research Professor of [[Physics]] at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA).<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.pa.ucla.edu/faculty-websites/gruner_bio.pdf|title=George Grüner Biography}}</ref> His research spans fundamental [[condensed matter physics]], [[nanotechnology]], [[bioelectronics]], and [[materials science]]. He has authored more than 700 publications with over 46,000 citations and an [[h-index]] of 94<ref>{{Cite web |title=GEORGE GRUNER |url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=1mgA1YgAAAAJ&hl=en |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=scholar.google.com}}</ref>, and holds more than two dozen issued [[Patent|patents]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://www.pa.ucla.edu/faculty-websites/gruner.html|title=George Grüner}}</ref>

==Education and career==
Grüner showed early aptitude in [[mathematics]], winning several national prizes while in high school and representing [[Hungary]] as a member of its [[International Mathematical Olympiad|Mathematics Olympic Team]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |title=KÜLHONI MAGYAR TUDÓSPORTRÉK |url=https://real.mtak.hu/188454/1/Gruner_Gyorgy_MTA_MTK_Eb_hirlevel_2020_12_15.pdf |website=real.mtak.hu/}}</ref>

He completed his undergraduate and graduate studies  in physics at [[Eötvös Loránd University]], [[Budapest]] (1961–1966), and was awarded the [[Candidate of Sciences]] degree in Budapest in 1972.<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
Grüner began his professional career as a Research Scientist at the Central Research Institute for Physics, Budapest (1966–1972), followed by a [[Postdoctoral researcher|postdoctoral]] appointment at [[Imperial College London]] (1972–1973). He returned to the Central Research Institute for Physics as Department Head (1973–1978).<ref name=":2" />

He joined the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] as a Visiting Scientist (1980–1981) and was appointed Professor of Physics in 1981, Distinguished Professor of Physics in 1987, and Distinguished Research Professor of Physics in 2021.<ref name=":1" />

During his tenure at UCLA, he held a visiting scientist position at several universitiesn worldwide, including  the [[Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research]], [[Stuttgart]], and held several innovation-related positions at [[Nanyang Technological University]], [[Singapore]].<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/george-gruner/|title=George Grüner|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation}}</ref>

==Research and contributions==
During his career, the focus of his research was on the collective behavior of electrons in matter, these underly the electrical properties of materials. His scientific activities include exploratory research, technology development, invention and innovation activity, intellectual property creation, startup companies, and as an advisor, the innovation ecosystem.<ref name=":4" />

=== Electron liquids ===
Grüner used [[Spectroscopy|spectroscopic]] methods to investigate the interactions between [[Electron|electrons]] in [[Metal|metals]] and [[Alloy|alloys]] and their consequences for [[Electrical resistivity and conductivity|electronic]] and [[Optical properties of materials|optical properties]].<ref name=":0" />

=== Density waves and electron crystals ===
Grüner conducted extensive experimental research on [[Density wave|density waves]] — a crystalline [[Electronic structure|electronic]]  state in metals — using [[Direct current|dc]], [[Alternating current|ac]], optical, and pulsed [[electric field]] techniques. He maintained a long-standing collaboration with [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel laureate]] [[John Bardeen]] to test theoretical models of the phenomenon experimentally.<ref>{{Cite journal|title=The dynamics of charge-density waves, G Grüner, Reviews of modern physics 60 (4), 1129 1988|journal = Reviews of Modern Physics|volume = 60|issue = 4|pages = 1129–1181|doi = 10.1103/RevModPhys.60.1129|year = 1988|last1 = Grüner|first1 = G.}}</ref>

=== Superconductors ===
Grüner's group explored the [[microwave]] and [[Millimeter wave|millimeter-wave]] properties of [[Superconductor|superconductors]], contributing both to the fundamental understanding of [[superconductivity]] , and the application potential of superconductors.<ref>{{Cite journal |date=1998 |editor-last=Grüner |editor-first=George |title=Millimeter and Submillimeter Wave Spectroscopy of Solids |url=https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/BFb0103417 |journal=Topics in Applied Physics |language=en |doi=10.1007/BFb0103417|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Nanotechnology and carbon nanonets ===
Grüner developed a novel class of materials called [[Nanonet|Nanonets]] — two-dimensional, interconnected random networks of nanowires: [[Single-walled carbon nanotube|single-walled carbon nanotubes]] which serve as a foundational platform for [[flexible electronics]]. His group characterized the electronic and optical properties of these structures.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last=Gruner |first=George |date=2007 |title=Carbon Nanonets Spark New Electronics |url=https://doi.org/10.1038/scientificamerican0507-76 |journal=Scientific American |volume=296 |issue=5 |pages=76–83 |doi=10.1038/scientificamerican0507-76 |issn=0036-8733|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

=== Bioelectronics ===
Grüner's laboratory developed electronic structures integrating [[Resistor|resistors]], [[Field-effect transistor|field-effect transistors]], and [[Electrochemical capacitor|electrochemical capacitors]] with biological environments such as [[blood serum]] and [[Buffer solution|buffer solutions]]. His group pioneered the use of [[Carbon nanotube|carbon nanotubes]] for real-time electronic detection of biological interactions. He also integrated living [[Cell (biology)|cells]] with active electronic platforms, laying groundwork for devices capable of monitoring and driving [[Cell signaling|cellular functions]], testing [[drug]] responses, and linking [[Neuron|nerve cells]] for complex signaling systems.<ref name=":0" />

== Technology development ==

=== Microwave and millimeter-wave spectroscopy ===
Grüner's group developed resonant structures, interference bridges, and phase-sensitive transmission measurement tools for characterizing materials at [[microwave]] and [[Millimeter wave|millimeter-wave]] frequencies. These instruments have been adopted by industry as standard characterization tools.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grüner |first=G. |last2=Zawadowski |first2=A. |date=1972 |title=Semiphenomenological model for the resonances and charge neutrality in dilute magnetic alloys |url=https://doi.org/10.1016/0038-1098(72)90483-8 |journal=Solid State Communications |volume=11 |issue=5 |pages=663–667 |doi=10.1016/0038-1098(72)90483-8 |issn=0038-1098|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Innovation and commercialization ==

=== Flexible and printed electronics ===
Grüner applied [[Carbon nanotube|carbon nanonet]] thin films as flexible electrode scaffolds, enabling early-generation flexible [[Organic light-emitting diode|organic light-emitting diodes]] (OLEDs), solution-processed [[Organic solar cell|organic solar cells]], and [[energy storage]] devices.<ref name=":4" />

=== Biosensors and detectors ===
His group developed electronic detection methods of the presence of biological species Notable demonstrations include the direct electronic detection of [[prostate-specific antigen]] (PSA) in serum and the tracking of enzymatic [[starch]] degradation.<ref name=":4" />

=== Patents ===
Grüner is the inventor or co-inventor of more than two dozen issued [[Patent|patents]] in the areas of [[nanoscale]] materials, [[energy storage]], energy generation, and [[Biosensor|biosensing.]]<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/inventor/george-gruner|title=George Gruner Inventions, Patents and Patent Applications – Justia Patents Search|website=patents.justia.com}}</ref>

== Entrepreneurship ==

* '''Nanomix Inc.''' (2001–2005): Served as [[Chief Technology Officer]] and     Chief Scientist, inventing and developing a nanoscale electronic [[biosensor]] detection     platform based on his UCLA research.
* '''Unidym  Inc.''' (founded 2004): Founded the company and served as [[Chief executive officer|CEO]], focusing on the industrial-scale     fabrication of [[carbon nanotube]]-based products, including nanonet thin films and components for [[printed electronics]], [[energy     storage]], and [[solar cell]] devices.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://californiananoeconomy.org/content/unidym|title=Unidym}}</ref>

== Advisory and editorial roles ==
Grüner has served as a consultant and advisor to universities, startup companies, [[Multinational corporation|multinational corporations]], and government and funding agencies in the [[United States]], [[Asia]], [[Europe]], and the [[Middle East]].<ref name=":3" />

He has held the following editorial positions:

* Editor-in-Chief, ''Journal  of Transitional Materials Research<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://iopscience.iop.org/journal/2053-1613/page/Editorial%20board|title=Editorial board, Translational Materials Research}}</ref>''
* Editorial  Board Member, ''[[Journal of Nanotechnology]]''<ref name=":1" />
* Editorial  Board Member, ''[[Bentham Science Publishers|Recent Patents in Nanotechnology]]''<ref name=":0" />

== Awards and honours ==

* [[World Economic Forum]] Technology  Pioneer Award (2004 and 2008): Grüner is the only individual     reported to have received this award on two separate occasions.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://web.worldbank.org/archive/website00818/WEB/OTHER/2004_TEC.HTM|title=World Economic Forum – 2004 Tech Pioneers|website=web.worldbank.org}}</ref>
* [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] (1998):  Awarded by the [[John Simon Guggenheim     Memorial Foundation]] for exceptional contributions to the [[natural sciences]].<ref name=":3" />
* [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt Senior American Scientist Award]] (1984): Granted by the [[Humboldt Foundation]] to internationally recognized scientists.
* Distinguished  Professor, [[Budapest University of Technology and Economics]].<ref name=":0" />

He served as an expert panelist and emerging technology lecturer at the [[World Economic Forum]] in [[Davos]] (2003, 2008)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.weforum.org/about/list-of-technology-pioneers-2008/|title=List of Technology Pioneers 2008|website=World Economic Forum}}</ref> and at the [[Global Competitiveness Forum]] in [[Riyadh]] (2009).

=== Memberships ===

* Fellow''',''' [[American Physical Society]] (elected 1987): Recognized for experimental studies of the [[Kondo effect|Kondo     problem]] and the dynamics of [[charge density wave]] and [[spin density wave]] ground states.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Honors and Award Winners |url=https://www.aps.org/funding-recognition/winners |access-date=2026-07-09 |website=www.aps.org |language=en}}</ref>
* Foreign  Member''',''' [[Hungarian Academy of Sciences]] (elected  1990).<ref name=":0" />

== Personal life ==
Grüner is married to Maria Grüner. After accepting his position at UCLA, the couple left [[Hungary]] and lost [[Hungarian nationality law|Hungarian citizenship]]; following Hungary's [[Transition to democracy in Hungary|political transition of 1990]], he became a dual [[Hungarian nationality law|Hungarian]]-[[United States nationality law|American]] citizen. They have a daughter, Dora, and a son, Daniel.<ref name=":0" />

Grüner is an [[art collector]]. The Grüner Collection has been exhibited in several museums and is considered a significant holding of [[Hungarian neo-avant-garde]] art.<ref name=":0" />
